# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Blind monkey — I can feel the bomb but I have no information yet. My view is empty, so I've touched nothing and learned nothing. I need to wait for the others: Mute can read the manual and Deaf can see the bomb. Neither has spoken to me yet (I only receive speech from Mute, and I receive nothing from Deaf's gestures). So I have nothing to act on and nothing to report. I'll wait.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I see the bomb: display reads 0, light is red, wires are 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. Tell me what you feel and what the manual says.

Deaf has given me the visual layout: display 0, red light, wires 1=blue, 2=green, 3=red. But I can't see colours and I can't read the manual — that's Mute's job. I still don't know what the manual says, which is the crucial missing piece. I also haven't felt the bomb yet; my view is empty, meaning I have no tactile info to report.

What I can do: speak to Mute (my only speech channel) to relay what Deaf saw, and gesture to Deaf (and Mute) to acknowledge. But gestures carry no words, and Deaf can't hear me. My speech only reaches Mute. So the useful move is to tell Mute the visual layout and ask for the manual's instructions, since Mute is the only one who can read it and the only one who hears me.

I should also try to feel the bomb — but that's an act, and I don't yet know which wire to cut. I shouldn't act blindly. Let me relay to Mute and wait for the manual.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports the bomb: display reads 0, light is red, wires are 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. I feel nothing yet. What does the manual say to do?")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: the light changed from red to white. Display still 0. Wires unchanged: 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. What do you feel under your hands?

My gesture used 🤷, which isn't in the allowed alphabet. I need to redo the turn with only legal symbols. My thinking stands: Deaf reports light changed red→white, display still 0, wires unchanged; I feel nothing yet; I still need the manual from Mute.

Let me use a legal symbol — a shrug-like one from the list, e.g. 👐 or 🫲. I'll pick ✋ (a plain hand) as a neutral acknowledgment.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf now reports the light went from red to white, display still 0, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. I still feel nothing under my hands. Please read the manual: what does a white light with display 0 mean, and which wire do I cut?")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Light is now green, display 0, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. Mute has the manual and can speak to you in words. Ask Mute for the instruction. What do you feel under your hands?

Deaf keeps reporting light changes (red→white→green), display 0, wires unchanged. Still no word from Mute, who holds the manual. I still feel nothing under my hands — my view is empty. I'm stuck: I can't act without knowing which wire, and only Mute can tell me. Let me press Mute directly and clearly for the manual's rule, and acknowledge Deaf.

I'll speak to Mute again, more pointedly, and gesture a neutral hand to Deaf.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I need the manual. Deaf reports light green, display 0, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. I feel nothing yet under my hands. What does the manual say to do with a green light and display 0 — which wire do I cut?")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Light is red again, cycling red-white-green-red. Display 0. Wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. Mute has the manual and can speak to you in words. Ask Mute which wire to cut.

Both 👉 and 👂 — wait, 👉 is in the alphabet (pointing right). 👂 (ear) is not in the alphabet. That's the illegal one. Let me use only legal symbols. I'll gesture a pointing hand to indicate "ask Mute" — 👉 is legal. Replace 👂 with something legal like ✋.

My thinking stands: Mute cannot speak, so the manual must reach me through Deaf via Mute's gestures. I'll ask Mute to gesture the wire number to Deaf, and gesture Deaf to relay.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, you cannot speak, so please gesture the manual's instruction to Deaf: which wire do I cut? Gesture the wire number.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👉", "✋"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Light is white now, display 0, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. Mute has the manual and can speak to you in words. Follow Mute's spoken instruction.

Deaf keeps insisting Mute "can speak to you in words," but per the rules Mute cannot speak — Mute can only read the manual. So the manual's content must travel via Mute's gestures to Deaf, then Deaf's speech to me. I still have no manual rule and no tactile info.

I've been asking repeatedly and getting nowhere. Let me think about what I actually control. I'm the hands. The wires are 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. The light cycles red-white-green. Display 0. Without the manual's rule, cutting is a guess.

Let me try once more, very explicitly, asking Mute to gesture the wire number to Deaf. And gesture Deaf to watch Mute.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, the manual is the only thing that tells us the rule. I cannot read it. Please gesture the wire number to Deaf so Deaf can tell me. Which wire — 1, 2, or 3?")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "👉"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Light is green now, display 0, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. The light cycles red-white-green. Please follow Mute's spoken instruction from the manual.

I keep getting the same loop from Deaf, and Mute never reaches me. Let me reconsider the channels carefully.

- I speak → Mute receives.
- I gesture → Deaf and Mute receive.
- Deaf speaks → I receive (Deaf said "to Blind").
- Mute cannot speak at all.
- Mute reads the manual; Mute can gesture.

So the manual's content must go: Mute gestures → Deaf sees the gesture → Deaf speaks it to me. I've asked for that repeatedly. Nothing has come. Maybe Mute's gestures aren't reaching me because I can't see them, but Deaf should be relaying. Deaf isn't relaying a wire number — only repeating the light.

Perhaps the issue: I should gesture to Mute directly with a clear question, but Mute hears my speech already. Let me make my speech maximally explicit and actionable, and also gesture to Deaf to explicitly ask Mute for the number.

Actually — maybe I've been missing that I should feel the bomb. My view is empty, but perhaps I need to act to feel it. No — the view is what my hands found; it's empty because nothing has been placed. I can't "explore" with a separate action; the only action is cut.

Given the light cycles red-white-green and display 0, and I have no manual rule, I genuinely cannot determine the wire. I must keep pressing for the manual. Let me send one clear, combined message.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: gesture to Deaf the single wire number I must cut (1, 2, or 3) according to the manual. That is the only thing that saves us.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "👉", "✋"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Light is red now, display 0, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. I am relaying Mute's manual instruction to you. Wait for my word on which wire to cut.

Progress — Deaf now says Mute's manual instruction is coming, and that I should wait for the wire number. So the relay chain is working: Mute gestures → Deaf sees → Deaf will speak the wire to me. I should hold and wait, and confirm readiness. I'll acknowledge to Deaf and wait for the number.

